logic_node.action: Implant ICD for primary prevention of SCD
logic_node.action_detail: In patients with nonischemic DCM or ischemic heart disease at least 40 days post-MI with LVEF <=35% and NYHA class II or III symptoms on chronic GDMT, who have reasonable expectation of meaningful survival for >1 year, ICD therapy is recommended for primary prevention of SCD to reduce total mortality.

logic_node.action: Implant ICD for primary prevention of SCD
logic_node.action_detail: In patients at least 40 days post-MI with LVEF <=30% and NYHA class I symptoms while receiving GDMT, who have reasonable expectation of meaningful survival for >1 year, ICD therapy is recommended for primary prevention of SCD to reduce total mortality.

logic_node.action_detail: For patients who have LVEF <=35%, sinus rhythm, LBBB with QRS duration >=150 ms, and NYHA class II, III, or ambulatory IV symptoms on GDMT, CRT is indicated to reduce total mortality, reduce hospitalizations, and improve symptoms and QOL.

source_text: For patients who have LVEF <= 35%, sinus rhythm, left bundle branch block (LBBB) with a QRS duration >= 150 ms, and NYHA class II, III, or ambulatory IV symptoms on GDMT, CRT is indicated

logic_node.action: Consider CRT for non-LBBB with QRS >=150 ms
logic_node.action_detail: For patients who have LVEF <=35%, sinus rhythm, a non-LBBB pattern with a QRS duration >=150 ms, and NYHA class II, III, or ambulatory class IV symptoms on GDMT, CRT can be useful to reduce total mortality, reduce hospitalizations, and improve symptoms and QOL.

source_text: For patients who have LVEF <= 35%, sinus rhythm, a non-LBBB pattern with a QRS duration >= 150 ms, and NYHA class II, III, or ambulatory class IV symptoms on GDMT, CRT can be useful

logic_node.action: Consider CRT for heart block with LVEF 36-50%
logic_node.action_detail: In patients with high-degree or complete heart block and LVEF of 36% to 50%, CRT is reasonable to reduce total mortality, reduce hospitalizations, and improve symptoms and QOL.

source_text: In patients with high-degree or complete heart block and LVEF of 36% to 50%, CRT is reasonable to reduce total mortality, reduce hospitalizations, and improve symptoms and QOL.

logic_node.action: Consider CRT for LBBB with QRS 120-149 ms
logic_node.action_detail: For patients who have LVEF <=35%, sinus rhythm, LBBB with a QRS duration of 120 to 149 ms, and NYHA class II, III, or ambulatory IV symptoms on GDMT, CRT can be useful to reduce total mortality, reduce hospitalizations, and improve symptoms and QOL.

source_text: For patients who have LVEF <= 35%, sinus rhythm, LBBB with a QRS duration of 120 to 149 ms, and NYHA class II, III, or ambulatory IV symptoms on GDMT, CRT can be useful

logic_node.action: Consider CRT in atrial fibrillation with LVEF <=35%
logic_node.action_detail: In patients with AF and LVEF <=35% on GDMT, CRT can be useful if: a) the patient requires ventricular pacing or otherwise meets CRT criteria and b) atrioventricular nodal ablation or pharmacological rate control will allow near 100% ventricular pacing with CRT.

source_text: In patients with AF and LVEF <= 35% on GDMT, CRT can be useful if: a) the patient requires ventricular pacing or otherwise meets CRT criteria and b) AV nodal ablation or pharmacological rate control will allow near 100% ventricular pacing

logic_node.action: Consider CRT when significant ventricular pacing anticipated
logic_node.action_detail: For patients on GDMT who have LVEF <=35% and are undergoing placement of a new or replacement device implantation with anticipated requirement for significant (>40%) ventricular pacing, CRT can be useful to reduce total mortality, reduce hospitalizations, and improve symptoms and QOL.

source_text: For patients on GDMT who have LVEF <= 35% and are undergoing placement of a new or replacement device with anticipated requirement for significant (>40%) ventricular pacing, CRT can be useful

logic_node.action: Consider ICD for genetic arrhythmogenic cardiomyopathy
logic_node.action_detail: In patients with genetic arrhythmogenic cardiomyopathy with high-risk features of sudden death, with EF <=45%, implantation of ICD is reasonable to decrease sudden death.

source_text: In patients with genetic arrhythmogenic cardiomyopathy with high-risk features of sudden death, with EF <= 45%, implantation of ICD is reasonable to decrease sudden death.

logic_node.action: Consider CRT for non-LBBB with QRS 120-149 ms and NYHA III-IV
logic_node.action_detail: For patients who have LVEF <=35%, sinus rhythm, a non-LBBB pattern with QRS duration of 120 to 149 ms, and NYHA class III or ambulatory class IV on GDMT, CRT may be considered to reduce total mortality, reduce hospitalizations, and improve symptoms and QOL.

source_text: For patients who have LVEF <= 35%, sinus rhythm, a non-LBBB pattern with QRS duration of 120 to 149 ms, and NYHA class III or ambulatory class IV on GDMT, CRT may be considered

logic_node.action: Consider CRT for ischemic NYHA I with LBBB >=150 ms
logic_node.action_detail: For patients who have LVEF <=30%, ischemic cause of HF, sinus rhythm, LBBB with a QRS duration >=150 ms, and NYHA class I symptoms on GDMT, CRT may be considered to reduce hospitalizations and improve symptoms and QOL.

source_text: For patients who have LVEF <= 30%, ischemic cause of HF, sinus rhythm, LBBB with a QRS duration >= 150 ms, and NYHA class I symptoms on GDMT, CRT may be considered

logic_node.action_detail: In patients with QRS duration <120 ms, CRT is not recommended.

source_text: In patients with QRS duration <120 ms, CRT is not recommended.

logic_node.action: Do not implant CRT for non-LBBB QRS <150 ms with NYHA I-II
logic_node.action_detail: For patients with NYHA class I or II symptoms and non-LBBB pattern with QRS duration <150 ms, CRT is not recommended.

source_text: For patients with NYHA class I or II symptoms and non-LBBB pattern with QRS duration <150 ms, CRT is not recommended.

logic_node.action: Do not implant ICD or CRT-D if survival <1 year
logic_node.action_detail: For patients whose comorbidities or frailty limit survival with good functional capacity to <1 year, ICD and CRT-D are not indicated.

source_text: For patients whose comorbidities or frailty limit survival with good functional capacity to <1 year, ICD and cardiac resynchronization therapy with defibrillation (CRT-D) are not indicated.

logic_node.action_detail: An implantable device that electrically stimulates the baroreceptors of the carotid artery has been FDA-approved for the improvement of symptoms in patients with advanced HF (NYHA class III, LVEF <=35%) who are unsuited for treatment with other HF devices including CRT. Associated with improvements in QOL, exercise capacity, and NT-proBNP levels.

source_text: An implantable device that electrically stimulates the baroreceptors of the carotid artery has been approved by the FDA for the improvement of symptoms in patients with advanced HF who are unsuited for treatment with other HF devices including CRT.

logic_node.action_detail: Cardiac contractility modulation (CCM) is FDA-approved for patients with NYHA class III with LVEF of 25% to 45% who are not candidates for CRT. RCTs have shown benefits in exercise capacity and QOL but no benefits in death or hospitalizations.

source_text: CCM is FDA-approved for patients with NYHA class III with LVEF of 25% to 45% who are not candidates for CRT. Four RCTs have shown benefits in exercise capacity and QOL but, as of yet, no benefits in death or hospitalizations.

logic_node.action_detail: In selected patients with HF, reduced EF (EF <=35%), and suitable coronary anatomy, surgical revascularization (CABG) plus GDMT is beneficial to improve symptoms, cardiovascular hospitalizations, and long-term all-cause mortality.

source_text: In selected patients with HF, reduced EF (EF <= 35%), and suitable coronary anatomy, surgical revascularization plus GDMT is beneficial to improve symptoms, cardiovascular hospitalizations, and long-term all-cause mortality.
